passages.text: As my Master used to say, “The vulture soars high out of sight in the sky, but his eye is ever on a bit of carrion on the earth.”
passages.note: lofty ideals undermined by petty attachments

passages.text: “Knowledge in books and money in other people’s hands is like no knowledge and no money at all.”
passages.note: knowledge must be lived, not merely stored

passages.text: The path of devotion is natural and pleasant. Philosophy is taking the mountain stream back to its force. It is a quicker method but very hard. Philospophy says, “Check everything.” Devotion says, “Give the stream, have eternal self-surrender.” It is a longer way, but easier and happier. “Thine am I for ever; henceforth whatever I do, it is Thou doing it. No more is there any me or mine.”
passages.note: surrender versus struggle on the spiritual path

passages.text: “Having no money to give, no brains to learn, no time to practice Yoga, to Thee, O sweet One, I give myself, to Thee my body and mind.”
passages.note: feeling inadequate; offering oneself as one is

passages.text: No amount of ignorance or wrong ideas can put a barrier between the soul and God. Even if there be no God, still hold fast to love. It is better to die seeking a God than as a dog seeking only carrion. Choose the highest ideal, and give your life up to that. “Death being so certain, it is the highest thing to give up life for a great purpose.”
passages.note: purpose, doubt, and holding fast to love

passages.text: Knowledge is critical and makes a great fuss over everything; but Love says, “God will show His real nature to me” and accepts all.

Rabbia, sick upon her bed, By two saints was visited — Holy Malik, Hassan wise — Men of mark in Moslem eyes. Hassan said, “Whose prayer is pure Will God’s chastisements endure.” Malik, from a deeper sense Uttered his experience: “He who loves his master ’s choice Will in chastisement rejoice.” Rabbia saw some selfish will In their maxims lingering still, And replied “O men of grace, He who sees his Master ’s face, Will not in his prayers recall That he is chastised at all !”
passages.note: illness and suffering transcended by love

passages.text: With all powers comes further misery, so kill desire. Getting any desire is like putting a stick into a nest of hornets.
passages.note: desire and ambition bring more suffering
